title: CS 480W/481: Senior Capstone Project
text:
Welcome
Welcome to the Senior Capstone Project sequence! This two-semester course represents the culmination of your computer science education, where you’ll design, develop, and deploy a significant software project from concept to completion.

title: CS 480W/481: Senior Capstone Project
text:
Course Overview
This capstone experience provides an opportunity to demonstrate your mastery of software engineering principles through the creation of a substantial application. You’ll engage in all phases of the software development lifecycle, applying industry-standard practices including requirements analysis, system design, implementation, testing, and deployment.
Throughout this journey, you’ll work independently on your chosen project while receiving guidance through regular consultations and peer collaboration. The course emphasizes not only technical excellence but also professional skills including project management, documentation, and effective communication of complex technical concepts.

Professor Fred Agbo, PhD

Office hours are available by 15-minute appointments or on a drop-in basis when available. Multiple modalities are offered (in-person, phone, Google Meet). If the scheduled times do not align with your availability, please contact the instructor.



A two-semester culminating experience where students apply their cumulative knowledge to design, develop, and deploy a full-stack or similar-type application. Students will follow industry-standard software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, from initial conception through final deployment and documentation. The course emphasizes professional software engineering methodology, project management, technical communication, and collaborative development practices.



Upon completion of this course sequence, students will be able to:

Design and implement a complete full-stack or similar-type application from conception to deployment
Apply software engineering principles and best practices throughout the development lifecycle
Demonstrate proficiency in project management and agile methodologies
Create comprehensive technical documentation
Present technical work to both technical and non-technical audiences
Collaborate effectively using version control and project management tools
Conduct meaningful peer reviews and incorporate feedback












Software Engineering: A Modern Approach
Marco Tulio Valente. Free, open textbook. Available at engsoftmoderna.info
Required


Handbook of Software Engineering Methods
Lara Letaw. Free OER via Open Textbook Library. Available at open.umn.edu
Required



Software Engineering: A Modern Approach provides comprehensive coverage of software engineering topics including process models, requirements, architecture, design, testing, and maintenance. Handbook of Software Engineering Methods complements it with a practical, methods-oriented framing aligned with real-world project work. Both texts are free and open-access.

title: CS 481W/482: Course Syllabus
text:
This course uses an agile-inspired methodology adapted for academic settings. The approach combines iterative development with structured academic milestones.
Core Principles: - Iterative Progress: Build features incrementally with regular feedback - Regular Cadence: Weekly development cycles aligned with instructor meetings - Continuous Integration: Regular code integration and automated testing - Flexible Planning: Adapt requirements based on learning and feedback - Active Engagement: Regular communication with instructor and peers

Version Control Standards: - Commit frequently (minimum daily when actively developing) - Use meaningful commit messages following conventional formats - Work in feature branches, merge via pull requests - Maintain a clean main branch with working code
Testing Requirements: - Write unit tests for core functionality - Implement integration tests for key workflows - Maintain reasonable code coverage (60%+ in Semester 2) - Document test cases and expected outcomes
Documentation Standards: - Maintain up-to-date README with setup instructions - Document API endpoints and data structures - Include inline code comments for complex logic - Keep a development journal tracking decisions and progress

title: CS 481W/482: Course Syllabus
text:
Each student engages in peer review activities throughout both semesters, providing feedback on two assigned projects while receiving feedback on their own.



Partnerships are established at the beginning of Fall semester and continue through Spring. This consistency allows reviewers to develop deep familiarity with each project.



Fall Semester Reviews: - Early draft feedback (proposal stage) - Architecture and design review - Code review sessions (backend and frontend) - Prototype evaluation
Spring Semester Reviews: - Feature implementation feedback - Testing strategy review - Deployment assessment - Final documentation review



Effective peer reviews include: - Specific feedback with examples - Constructive suggestions for improvement - Recognition of strengths - Questions that promote deeper thinking - Timely submission

title: CS 481W/482: Course Syllabus
text:
Your project proposal should include:
Executive Summary (1 page): - Project title and brief description - Problem being addressed - Proposed solution overview - Target users or audience
Technical Details (2-3 pages): - Functional requirements (at least 10) - Non-functional requirements (performance, security, etc.) - Technology stack with justification - System architecture overview
Project Management (1-2 pages): - Development approach and methodology - Timeline with key milestones - Risk analysis and mitigation strategies - Success criteria
Research and References (1 page): - Analysis of similar existing solutions - Key technical resources - New technologies or skills to be learned

title: CS 481W/482: Course Syllabus
text:
All submitted work must be your own or properly attributed. Use of AI tools must be documented. Plagiarism or academic dishonesty will result in serious consequences including possible course failure. Consult your institution’s academic integrity policy for complete details.



Students have a cumulative bank of 72 hours (3 days) for late submissions throughout both semesters. These hours can be allocated across any deliverables as needed. Once this bank is exhausted, late work receives a 20% penalty per 24-hour period. Work more than 5 days late receives no credit. Contact the instructor immediately if extenuating circumstances arise.



Incomplete grades are granted only in cases of serious illness, family emergency, or other circumstances beyond student control that prevent completion of coursework. Incompletes are not granted for time management difficulties or falling behind. Students experiencing challenges should contact the instructor early to develop a support plan.



This is an intensive course requiring substantial work outside of scheduled meetings. Expect to dedicate 8-12 hours per week to project development, documentation, and related activities. Consistent weekly effort is essential for success.



Students requiring academic accommodations should provide appropriate documentation from your institution’s accessibility office within the first two weeks of the semester. The instructor will work with you to ensure appropriate support.




Weekly meetings are mandatory except in case of emergency
Use approved communication channels for questions and updates
Response time: instructor will respond within 24-48 hours during business days
For urgent issues, use designated emergency contact method

Modified Agile with Academic Milestones
This course employs a Modified Agile methodology that combines industry-standard Agile practices with academic milestone requirements.

Core Principles

Iterative Development: Features built incrementally with regular feedback loops
Weekly Sprints: One-week development cycles aligned with instructor meetings
Continuous Integration: Code integrated and tested regularly
Adaptive Planning: Requirements evolve based on feedback and learning
Stakeholder Engagement: Instructor as product owner (or external customer in certain situations) and peers as stakeholders

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Academic Integrity
All code must be original or properly attributed. AI tool usage must be documented. Plagiarism results in course failure. For details, consult Willamette’s academic integrity policy.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Late Work
Students are allotted 72 cumulative hours (3 days) of late submissions across all deliverables without penalty. Hours may be distributed across assignments as needed. Once exhausted, late submissions incur a 20% penalty per 24 hours on a continuous scale; deliverables submitted more than 5 days late receive no credit. Extenuating circumstances should be discussed with the instructor promptly.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Incomplete Grades
Incomplete grades are granted only for prolonged illness or family emergencies that remove a student from the learning environment for an extended period. Incompletes are not granted for falling behind due to motivation, comprehension, or time management difficulties. Students experiencing academic difficulties should consult with the instructor to develop an improvement plan.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Time Commitment
Per Willamette’s Credit Hour Policy, each hour of class time requires 2–3 hours of work outside class. The advanced nature of this course requires consistent effort throughout the semester. Expect 6–9 hours per week of outside engagement including development, documentation, and project work.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Classroom Conduct
Constructive classroom behavior supports an environment of trust, respect, and collaborative learning. Disruptive behaviors include but are not limited to: interrupting others, distracting from course content, unauthorized recordings, and any form of harassment or abuse. Such behaviors will not be tolerated.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Accommodations
Students requiring accommodations should provide documentation from Accessible Education Services (Smullin 155, 503-370-6737, accessible-info@willamette.edu) within the first two weeks.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Inclusive Classroom
Students are addressed by their affirmed name and pronouns upon request. Notify the instructor at any point to update records accordingly.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Accessibility and Accommodations
Willamette University is committed to creating inclusive learning environments. Students experiencing barriers to inclusion or achievement should notify the instructor promptly. Students with disabilities are encouraged to contact Accessible Education Services (Smullin 155, 503-370-6737, accessible-info@willamette.edu) to discuss accommodations.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Title IX
Willamette University prohibits discrimination and harassment based on sex or gender. As a mandatory reporter, the instructor is required to report any incidents of sexual misconduct disclosed to them to Willamette’s Title IX Coordinator. For confidential support, contact:

Confidential advocate: confidential-advocate@willamette.edu
WUTalk crisis line: 503-375-5353
Campus Safety (emergency): 503-370-6911

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Religious Accommodations
Students requiring accommodations for religious observances should notify the instructor within the first two weeks of the semester.

title: CS 480W/481: Course Syllabus
text:
Land Acknowledgement
We respectfully acknowledge that Willamette University is located on the ancestral lands of the Kalapuya people, who today are represented by the Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde and the Confederated Tribes of the Siletz Indians. We honor their deep connection to this land and recognize the ongoing contributions of Indigenous peoples to our academic community.

Course materials structure adapted from Dr. Lucas P. Cordova’s CS Capstone course. Special thanks to Lucas for the excellent organizational framework to capstone education.

Note: This syllabus is subject to change with reasonable notice. Students will be informed of any significant changes via official communication channels.
